newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Riksbank poll shows 49 pct Swedes against ERM.
newsitem.headline: Riksbank poll shows 49 pct Swedes against ERM.

text.p: Sweden's central bank, the Riksbank, said on Monday a poll showed that 49 percent of Swedes were against linking the crown to the European Union's Exchange Rate Mechanism (ERM).
"The figure is virtually the same for every social group, irrespective of sex, age and occupation," the Riksbank said in statement.
It said 22 percent of Swedes were in favour of ERM participation, the survey showed.
The survey of 1,000 Swedes aged between 16 and 74 was carried out in the first two weeks of December, 1996. The margin of error ranged from +/- 1.4 to 3.2 percentage points.
A poll also showed that 60 percent of Swedes supported the Riksbank's target of two percent inflation, while 12 percent were opposed to the target.
The proportion of people who believed the Riksbank would achieve its inflation target rose to 50 percent from 27 percent at the time of an earlier survey in March last year.

Fifty percent of those surveyed said the Riksbank conducted monetary policy in the right way, while 11 percent said it did not. Of those who had a definite view, 82 percent were in favour of the Riksbank's monetary policy.
The Riksbank said the surveys were carried out to measure what Swedes know about their central bank.
